subject: E-Commerce
title: Direct-to-Consumer Peaks
description: A fast breakdown of Direct-to-Consumer Peaks for builders.

hook.text: Casper, Allbirds, and Away were DTC darlings. All three saw stocks crash 80%+ after going public. The model hit a wall.

buildup.text: DTC promised to cut out middlemen: sell directly online, keep the margin, own the customer relationship.

discovery.text: Customer acquisition costs on Facebook and Instagram tripled between 2019 and 2023.

twist.text: DTC brands now sell on Amazon and in Walmart. They returned to the middlemen they were supposed to replace.

climax.text: DTC worked when ads were cheap. When customer acquisition costs rise, every direct seller faces the same economics.

punchline.text: 80% stock crashes, back on Amazon. DTC was channel arbitrage, not a moat.

quiz.question: Why did many direct-to-consumer brands struggle after their initial success?
options: Customer acquisition costs on social media tripled, breaking the unit economics
